title: How many continuing education hours do insurance adjusters need in Florida?
description: Florida adjuster CE: the 4 hour law and ethics update plus 20 elective hours every 2 years, public adjuster limits and reciprocity under section 626.2815.
shortAnswer: Florida requires licensed insurance adjusters to complete 24 hours of continuing education every two years: a 4 hour law and ethics update course specific to adjusters, plus 20 elective hours. The rule is section 626.2815, Florida Statutes, administered by the Florida Department of Financial Services (DFS). Electives drop to 16 hours after 6 years of licensure, and public adjusters must choose electives from a restricted list of approved course types.
keyTakeaways: Section 626.2815(2) applies CE to everyone licensed to adjust insurance claims in Florida for lines that require a licensing exam, and to the insurers, employers and appointing entities involved.

Every licensee except title agents must take a 4 hour update course every 2 years specific to the license held (626.2815(3)); for adjusters other than public adjusters this is course authority 5-620, and for public adjusters 5-320.
Elective hours are 20 every 2 years (626.2815(3)(a)), 16 after 6 or more years of licensure (3)(b), and 6 for 25 year licensees holding a CLU, CPCU or qualifying degree (3)(c).
For CE cycles ending on or after July 31, 2023, DFS accepts public adjuster electives only from listed course authorities covering property, adjusting law, ethics and mitigation.

Excess hours carry forward to the next period (3)(g), DFS may extend the deadline by up to 1 year for good cause (5), and it may terminate or refuse to renew the appointment of a noncompliant adjuster (9).
regulator: Florida Department of Financial Services (DFS), under section 626.2815 of the Florida Statutes
appliesTo: Resident all-lines adjusters licensed in Florida
Public adjusters, except those limited to workers' compensation or health insurance
Nonresident all-lines adjusters whose home state is not on Florida's CE reciprocity list, and all designated home state (DHS) adjusters
Insurers, employers and appointing entities, for whom CE compliance is a condition of appointment

sections.heading: How many CE hours does a Florida adjuster need?

blocks.text: A Florida adjuster needs 24 hours every two years, made up of a 4 hour law and ethics update course for adjusters and 20 hours of electives. The rule is [section 626.2815, Florida Statutes](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0600-0699/0626/Sections/0626.2815.html), and the [DFS continuing education chart for licensees](https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/agents/education/licensees) breaks it down by license type, as at November 2026.

blocks.text: The update course content is set by statute. Section 626.2815(3) requires it to address insurance law updates, ethics for insurance professionals, disciplinary trends and case studies, industry trends, premium discounts, determining suitability of products and services, and other topics DFS considers relevant. A licensee holding several licenses needs an update course for at least one of them.

sections.heading: Can an experienced adjuster complete fewer hours?

blocks.text: Yes. Reductions apply to the elective hours only; the 4 hour update course is always required. DFS notes that its chart does not show reductions and that they are applied to the elective category.

items: **6 or more years licensed:** a minimum of 16 elective hours every 2 years (626.2815(3)(b)), for 20 total.

**25 or more years licensed with a designation or degree:** a licensee who is a CLU or CPCU, or holds a bachelor's degree or higher in risk management or insurance with 18 or more semester hours of insurance courses, needs a minimum of 6 elective hours (626.2815(3)(c)).
**Association participation:** up to 2 elective hours per calendar year may be approved for active participation in an association, if the association reports it (626.2815(3)(j)).

**Designation programs:** completing part of the Claims and Litigation Management Alliance Universal Claims Certification counts for 20 elective hours and the 4 hours required under subsection (3) (626.2815(7)(i)).

sections.heading: What extra rules apply to public adjusters?

blocks.text: Public adjusters must take their own update course and choose electives from a narrower field. Section 626.2815(3)(f) limits public adjuster electives to courses related to commercial and residential property coverages, claim adjusting practices and other adjuster electives approved by DFS, and exempts public adjusters for workers' compensation or health insurance from the CE requirement entirely.

DFS applies this through course authorities. For CE cycles ending on or after July 31, 2023, a public adjuster (license type 3-20) can satisfy elective credits only with courses approved under the listed authorities: General Lines (Property and Casualty), Public Adjuster Law and Policy, Public Adjuster Ethics, Public Adjuster Optional, Adjuster Law and Policy, Adjuster Ethics, Adjuster Optional, the three law and ethics update authorities, and Premium Discounts and Mitigation Options. A public adjuster's training plan should be built from that list rather than from the general elective catalog.

sections.heading: Do nonresident and DHS adjusters need Florida CE?

blocks.text: Nonresident all-lines adjusters can usually rely on CE completed in a reciprocal state, but every designated home state adjuster must complete Florida's requirement. Section 626.2815(6) lets a nonresident use home state CE if the home state reciprocates with Florida, and requires Florida CE where the home state has no requirement and no reciprocal alternative exists.

DFS publishes a nonresident all-lines adjuster reciprocity list with a continuing education reciprocity column. A nonresident who has completed CE in a state marked yes does not need Florida CE, and DFS periodically checks the National Insurance Producers Registry (NIPR) for the standing of the adjuster's other licenses. DFS states that the list does not apply to the nonresident public adjuster license or to the DHS adjuster license, and that all holders of a Florida DHS adjuster license must complete Florida's CE requirements.

sections.heading: What happens if an adjuster does not complete CE on time?

blocks.text: Noncompliance puts the adjuster's appointment at risk. Section 626.2815(4) makes CE compliance a condition precedent to the issue, continuation, reinstatement or renewal of any appointment, and section 626.2815(9) lets DFS immediately terminate or refuse to renew the appointment of an adjuster notified that their CE has not been certified, unless an extension or waiver has been granted.

items: **Extension:** for good cause DFS may grant more time, but no more than 1 year (626.2815(5)).
**Military waiver:** licensees unable to comply because of active military duty may request a written waiver (626.2815(2)).
**Reinstatement block:** after a renewal appointment is denied for missing CE, DFS will not issue a new appointment of the same or similar type until the CE is completed (626.2815(9)).
**Carry forward:** excess hours from one 2 year compliance period may be carried into the next (626.2815(3)(g)), which is unusual among state regimes.
**Update course transition:** DFS began enforcing the 4 hour update requirement for cycles ending on or after January 31, 2022; earlier outstanding cycles used the previous 5 hour update course.

sections.heading: Which courses count, and who keeps the records?

blocks.text: Courses must be DFS-approved and, unless an exception applies, delivered by classroom instruction or ending in a monitored examination. Section 626.2815(7)(k) exempts interactive online courses with sufficient internal testing and paper self-study courses with a closed book final exam, which may be unproctored if supported by a sworn affidavit.

Providers must report completions within 21 days in a form DFS accepts (626.2815(8)), and DFS says licensees should not submit certificates unless asked. Providers must keep attendance records for five years, and licensees should keep their own certificate copies. Responsibility for choosing the right course and avoiding duplicate courses sits with the licensee, who can monitor compliance in their DFS MyProfile account. The [guide to preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) explains how to hold certificates against the requirement they satisfy.

sections.heading: How should a carrier or adjusting firm track Florida compliance?

blocks.text: Because appointment depends on CE, firms that deploy adjusters in Florida, especially after a hurricane, need to know before deployment who is compliant. The table maps each obligation to the person, the timing and the evidence.

blocks.text: Texas, the other large catastrophe market, uses a different structure with classroom minimums and per-hour fines; see the page on [Texas insurance adjuster continuing education](/regulations/texas-insurance-adjuster-continuing-education). Agent CE in Florida runs under the same statute and is summarized on the page on [insurance producer continuing education requirements](/regulations/insurance-producer-continuing-education-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry holds Florida's update course, elective reductions and public adjuster course authorities as rules attached to each adjuster role. Claims procedures and ethics content are mapped to those rules, so a firm can show which requirement each completed course satisfies when an appointment is reviewed.

faqs.q: Do crop insurance agents fall under Florida's CE rule?
faqs.a: No, if they hold only the limited license. Section 626.2815(2) excludes individuals who hold a limited license as a crop or hail and multiple-peril crop insurance agent, and licenses for lines that do not require an exam. Federal crop program training for agents and loss adjusters is set separately by the Standard Reinsurance Agreement.

faqs.q: Can I use the same update course for an agent license and an adjuster license?
faqs.a: A licensee holding multiple licenses must complete an update course specific to at least one license held, under section 626.2815(3). For adjusters other than public adjusters, DFS lists course authority 5-620 as the corresponding 4 hour update course.

Yes, if DFS approved them. Section 626.2815(7)(k) allows interactive online independent study with sufficient internal testing to validate comprehension, without a monitored examination. Other self-study formats need a closed book final exam meeting DFS rules.

faqs.q: Can extra hours reduce my next cycle?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 626.2815(3)(g) allows excess hours accumulated during a 2 year compliance period to be carried forward to the next compliance period. The 4 hour update course is still required in every 2 year period.
